summary.intent: Act as orchestrator/PM for CipherBox v2, delegating implementation of the #635 rotation subsystem (and related engine/API slices) to background subagents, driving each draft PR through a mandatory review trio plus CodeRabbit/Greptile bot reviews, and performing large-scale repo housekeeping (issue hygiene, GitHub sub-issues/labels, stale artifact cleanup).
summary.outcome: Merged the full rotation build (Slices 1-4, eager cascade, cold-start data path, grant creation, resolver binding) plus several hardening PRs (#761,#742,#743,#748,#767-adjacent work), completed extensive GitHub housekeeping (labels, sub-issue trees, tag/release/deployment purge, comment-discipline AGENTS.md update), and caught/fixed a P0 main-breaking compile error caused by two independently-merged PRs conflicting on a shared struct field.

repo: Rotation model: rotateScope (read-plane root cut + eager cascade on revocation), sweep (idempotent lazy-wave, metadata-only, prev:None), rotateScopeWrite (owner-only write rotation, child-first name wave) — sweep must NEVER be used for revocation completion, only fresh-seed cascade closes that guarantee

Floor law: read-epoch regression check is sound ONLY at the owner-authored root/vault anchor; shared scopes legitimately unseal-advance past minReadEpoch (checking there is a self-inflicted DoS). Write-epoch floor is never unseal-advanced so its check is sound everywhere — encoded via AnchorRole{Root,Shared}

A resolved scope-root record carries no self-identifying scope_id (ChildScopeRef={scope_id,ipns_name}); binding scope_id to a record rests entirely on which scope_id the caller feeds the gate — the fix pattern is to drop scope_id from seam Target structs entirely so the enumerated child.scope_id is the sole authority (mirrors the pre-existing parent_node_seed omission)

CR (CodeRabbit) is org-wide rate-limited ~1/hr; drains after ~55-65min of zero triggers; a real review consumes the slot. Flip draft->ready to trigger it, then flip back to draft quickly if a fold needs to happen so the next push doesn't burn a second slot the moment CI settles
GitHub sub-issues API: POST repos/R/issues/<parent#>/sub_issues -F sub_issue_id=<child DB id> (child DB id via gh api repos/R/issues/<child#> -q .id, requires -F not -f for the integer)
Closes #NNN in a PR body auto-closes a dedicated issue on squash-merge; Part of #NNN is inert (correct for umbrellas) — the recurring issue-pileup bug was using Part of on dedicated issues
zsh does not word-split unquoted $var — must use explicit arrays arr=(...) and "${arr[@]}" for loops over ids/lists
Repo config commit.gpgsign=false — agent commits must use --no-verify, never -S or --no-gpg-sign
git-over-HTTPS and sometimes gh api are DNS-sandboxed in this environment; use dangerouslyDisableSandbox:true for git network ops and flaky gh calls
isolation:worktree forks LOCAL HEAD, not origin — must FF local main before launching a new build agent or it forks stale

Nested subagents can collide inside a shared (non-worktree-isolated) checkout: a helper's git checkout HEAD + cargo fmt --all can clobber a parent agent's uncommitted WIP — always isolate concurrent Rust-editing agents in separate worktrees

TypeORM forbids per-migration transaction=false under default migrationsTransactionMode:'all' (needed for CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY) — must set migrationsTransactionMode:'each' on all DataSources (CLI + test harness) as the required opt-out

code.finding: Bug: set plan.identity.scope_id = target.scope_id (resolver-returned) while the ascent-link seed derives under the enumerated child.scope_id (lines 528-529) and visited{} keys on child.scope_id (line 511) — a resolver returning a divergent scope_id would re-key/publish the wrong scope. Fixed by dropping scope_id from CascadeTarget entirely.

Post-#779 main broke: referenced SweepTarget.ipns_name at both lines, but #779 removed that field from SweepTarget in the same merge window as #782 added these call sites (both PRs individually green/mergeable, combined tree didn't compile). Hotfixed to use the enumerated descendant.ipns_name (ChildScopeRef.ipns_name) instead.

Mailbox idempotency key was format!("grant:{}", hex_lower(&grantee.scope_id)) — deterministic and low-entropy, causing a ZK sharing-graph leak since the API stores idempotencyScope=sha256(senderPk:idempotencyKey); two recipients of the same folder produced identical stored hashes, correlatable by the server. Fixed to bind the per-recipient blinded tag instead.

flagged_indexes.push ran before the CAS publish succeeded, so a LostRace reported a phantom index repair that never actually published. Fixed by moving the push into the Ok(()) arm, symmetric with the existing converged bookkeeping.

Security review found a MEDIUM: post-flip-crash resume built the interior retire list unconditionally from the resolver's reported current_name, which on resume reflects already-migrated names, causing retire to delete live migrated names. Fixed by only retiring names differing from the freshly-derived new name.

workflow: Always delegate the entire /resolve-pr-reviews flow (fetch->triage->fix->push->reply->resolve->report) to a single subagent and relay its report — splitting triage into the main thread wastes context and adds hops without benefit
When two crypto reviewers disagree on a finding, verify against the actual ground-truth source (e.g. real API code) rather than trusting either reviewer's confidence level

Partition parallel-launch candidates strictly by shared-code dependency, not just file path — two 'disjoint' slices needing the same not-yet-built helper function will collide; land the shared helper first or fold it into one of the two PRs

Reserve scarce CR review slots for genuinely trust/crypto/durability-critical PRs (already covered by trio+Greptile is often sufficient for lower-risk PRs); explicitly weigh CR ROI before spending a slot

After merging multiple individually-green PRs that touch the same struct/interface, immediately verify the combined main branch still compiles — textual mergeability does not guarantee semantic/type compatibility across concurrently-developed branches
Decouple CR-trigger-pacing (rate-limit backoff, ~55-65min) from review-completion-detection (a cheap read-poll every ~10min) — conflating them causes reviews to sit unactioned for hours

AGENTS.md comment-discipline rule needed concrete elaboration beyond 'no workaround apologia' — added two named smells (absence-justifying comments describing paths not in the diff; unchanged-code apologia defending untouched functions) plus a length discipline (state each invariant once, cross-reference the spec, headers over ~25 lines are a smell)

friction: Multiple subagent API stalls ('Response stalled mid-stream') mid-edit or mid-fold, requiring manual verification of actual git state before deciding whether to resume or restart the agent
statusCheckRollup via gh pr view reported stale/duplicate failed checks; had to cross-check the check-runs API on the exact head SHA to get ground truth

CR's incremental review cache sometimes refused to re-review already-seen commits, requiring @coderabbitai full review to force a real pass, which itself sometimes hit the rate limit and only posted an ack, not an actual review — required reading exact timestamp order to distinguish rate-limited-ack from a clean review
gh pr edit fails outright on this repo due to legacy Projects-classic integration — must patch PR bodies via gh api -X PATCH .../pulls/N -F body=@file
Harness-locked worktrees sometimes refuse --force removal and must be left for the harness's own lifecycle

Entire (the checkpoint/commit tool) doesn't track background-subagent worktree commits (they use --no-verify and never touch the main tree), making it look like nothing was checkpointing during heavy fan-out sessions — purely a visibility gap, not a real risk since all work is pushed to PR branches
